_note_field: MAINTAINER-ONLY. `note` records why a card is modelled the way it is -- provenance, schema reasoning, what was deliberately not modelled. Never render it in the UI. `caution` is the user-facing field.
_business_note: `business` marks a card issued on business underwriting rather than personal. Absent means personal -- only the field's presence is meaningful, so there is nothing to keep in sync on thirty-six records. It filters the catalogue and nothing else reads it: the ranker does not care whose name is on the account.
_common_note: `common` is a POPULARITY RANK, 1 to 40, and it is EDITORIAL. There is no public card-level ranking of US cardholders -- Nilson publishes issuer volume, not how many people hold a Freedom Unlimited -- so this is judgement, not a sourced fact, and it is the only field here that is. It orders the setup picker so a new user meets mass-market cards first. 21 to 40 were added on 2026-09-27 as the next twenty after the first, so they rank below all of it by construction. Re-rank it freely; nothing computes from it.

discover-it-chrome.note: The page now names Capital One as the party that classifies purchases, after its acquisition of Discover; the card is still sold under the Discover name. Gas includes 'some public electric vehicle charging stations', hence the ev_charging rule and its caveat. U.S. merchants only.

rules.caveat: Stand-alone gas stations. The $1,000 quarterly cap is combined with restaurants.
Some public EV charging stations only. The $1,000 quarterly cap is combined with gas and restaurants.
Includes restaurant delivery services. The $1,000 quarterly cap is combined with gas.

chase-freedom-rise.name: Chase Freedom Rise
chase-freedom-rise.note: Modelled as 'ur' for the reason Freedom Unlimited is: the offer details say cash back is tracked as points, 100 to the dollar, under chase.com/ultimaterewards. At the default 1.5 cpp that values the 1.5% at 2.25%, which only holds if you hold a Sapphire card to move the points to -- override the valuation in Options if you do not. Network read off the card art.

chase-ink-business-unlimited.name: Chase Ink Business Unlimited
chase-ink-business-unlimited.note: Currency 'ur' for the reason Ink Business Cash gives. The Lyft rate is modelled exactly as Ink Business Cash's is. Network read off the card art.

rules.caveat: Lyft rides only, and it is 5% TOTAL rather than a bonus on top. Offer ends 2027-09-30.

chase-ink-business-preferred.name: Chase Ink Business Preferred
chase-ink-business-preferred.caution: Business card. The 3X stops at $150,000 of combined spend in its categories per account anniversary year.
chase-ink-business-preferred.note: Rates and the 3X list read off the offer details 2026-09-27; category definitions off chase.com/RewardsCategoryFAQs the same day. Chase's travel covers airlines, hotels, car rental agencies, cruise lines, travel agencies, rail, taxis, tolls and parking -- every travel category Caddy has, OTAs included, so no denylist. 'Internet, cable and phone services' spans both phone and internet_cable. Advertising counts only when bought directly from a social media site or search engine, and shipping means couriers, postal and freight services. Network read off the card art.

rules.caveat: The $150,000 cap is combined across every 3X category, and runs per account anniversary year.

amex-blue-business-plus.name: Amex Blue Business Plus
amex-blue-business-plus.caution: Business card. The 2X stops at $50,000 of purchases a calendar year; after that everything earns 1X.
amex-blue-business-plus.note: No rules by design: 2X is the card's rate on everything, so it is the base rate. The $50,000 calendar-year limit cannot sit on a base rate, which has no cap field, so it lives in the caution -- and Caddy tracks no spend, so it could not apply the cap anyway.
